text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. speaker: Doctor
text: That diagnosis doesn't align with your fever, acute wrist swelling, and skin lesions. Based on your Minnesota camping trip and the specific description of painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions, this presentation is highly suggestive of Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever. I need to confirm this immediately; please tell me if you have a rash on your ankles or wrists that started at the wrists and is moving toward the center of your body. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR), and Urine Culture. REQUEST IMAGES: Full body skin examination photos.
